items.title: Depressive symptoms among adult patients with systemic lupus erythematosus in the Jazan Region, Saudi Arabia: An analytical cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Mental disorders, including depression, are common among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Depressive symptoms can significantly impair quality of life and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Studies investigating depressive symptoms and their associated factors in individuals with SLE have yielded inconsistent findings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms among patients with SLE and to identify the associated factors in patients from the Jazan Region of Saudi Arabia. An analytical cross-sectional study of 112 patients with SLE in Jazan, Saudi Arabia was conducted in 2023. A convenience sampling technique was used to recruit all eligible adult patients with SLE who attended rheumatology clinics and day-care units at the referral hospitals in the region. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Chi-square tests and binary logistic regression analyses were used to examine associations and identify factors associated with depressive symptoms. The majority of participants were female (104 [92.9%]), with ages ranging from 18 to 59 years. Depressive symptoms were present in 80% of participants, with patients experiencing mild depression 25 (22%), moderate depression 28 (25%), moderate-to-severe depression 22 (20%), and severe depression 15 (13%).In the multivariable analysis, although physical activity as a categorical variable did not reach overall statistical significance (global p = 0.067), participants engaging in less than 150 minutes of physical activity per week were significantly less likely to experience depressive symptoms compared with those performing no physical activity (OR = 0.28; 95% CI 0.10-0.82; P = 0.020).In conclusion, depressive symptoms were highly prevalent among patients with SLE in the Jazan Region, and physical activity level was identified as a significant modifiable associated factor in this population. Routine screening could facilitate early detection and intervention in patients with SLE in similar settings, resulting in improved clinical outcomes.

items.title: Myositis as a rare forerunner of Behçet's disease: insights from a new case and review of the literature to unmask a diagnostic trap.
items.abstract: Behcet's disease (BD) is a multisystemic vasculitis classically characterized by a triad of recurrent oral aphtosis, genital ulcers and uveitis. Muscular involvement is rare (described in only about 0.5-3% of cases) and often underrecognized. We report a 59 year old man admitted to our department for myositis, diarrhea, and elevated CPK without mucocutaneous signs. MRI (Magnetic resonance imaging) showed muscle edema, colonscopy reveal intestinal mucosal hyperemia, multiple aphthous ulcers on his sigmoid colon, mild edema and petechiae. BD was diagnosed in one years of follow up when the patient developed oral aphtosis, genital ulcers and HLA-B51 positivity was detected. This case underscores the diagnostic challenge when muscle involvement precedes classical features, complicating the differential diagnosis, and highlights the need to consider BD in unexplained myositis, especially in patients with gastrointestinal symptoms and HLA-B51 positivity. A review of 34 published cases on myositis as an initial manifestation of BD is provided.

items.title: Platelet CLEC-2 as an amplifier of synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Platelets have well-established roles in hemostasis and thrombosis and are increasingly recognized as active regulators of inflammation and immune responses. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), experimental and clinical studies have implicated platelets in synovial inflammation. Platelet depletion markedly attenuates arthritis in the K/BxN serum-transfer mouse model, and collagen-dependent glycoprotein VI (GPVI) signaling promotes platelet microparticle production, which activates fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) through interleukin-1 (IL-1). More recently, we reported that platelet C-type lectin-like receptor 2 (CLEC-2) promotes proliferation of fibroblast-like synoviocytes derived from patients with RA (RA-FLSs) in vitro and induces the expression of inflammatory mediators, including IL-6. In the same mouse model, platelet- and megakaryocyte-specific CLEC-2 deficiency suppressed arthritis progression without substantially affecting disease onset. These findings support a role for platelet CLEC-2 in the amplification rather than the initiation of synovial inflammation. This review focuses on the emerging role of platelet CLEC-2 in RA and its relationship with podoplanin-positive FLSs. We discuss platelet access to the synovial compartment, CLEC-2-dependent FLS responses, and the possible relationship between CLEC-2 and other platelet-dependent pathways in synovial inflammation. Taken together, current evidence supports a role for platelet CLEC-2 as an amplifier of ongoing synovial inflammation.

items.title: Identification of IFI44L as a potential immune-associated molecule and theoretical CAR-T target for systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-platform bioinformatic analysis.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a highly heterogeneous autoimmune disorder characterized by disrupted immune homeostasis, persistent chronic inflammation, and progressive multi-organ injury, accompanied by frequent disease flares and marked interindividual clinical heterogeneity. At present, specific molecular biomarkers for precise evaluation of immune dysregulation and guidance for individualized targeted therapy for SLE remain scarce. This study aimed to screen core genes associated with SLE, explore the correlation between IFI44L and SLE-associated immune disturbance, and validate its diagnostic performance, so as to provide bioinformatic evidence for precise immune diagnosis and targeted intervention of SLE. The GSE72326 microarray dataset was used as the training cohort to screen differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between SLE patients and healthy controls. Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analyses were performed to identify core hub genes. The CIBERSORTx algorithm was adopted to quantify peripheral blood immune cell infiltration. Spearman correlation analysis was conducted to assess the association between hub gene expression and immune cell infiltration, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate gene diagnostic efficacy. An independent RNA-seq cohort GSE211700 was used for cross-platform external validation of IFI44L expression patterns and diagnostic efficacy. A total of 104 SLE-related DEGs, including 93 upregulated and 11 downregulated genes, were identified with distinct expression patterns capable of distinguishing SLE patients from healthy controls. Functional enrichment results revealed that DEGs were predominantly enriched in type I interferon response, innate immune activation and inflammatory signaling cascades, consistent with the well-recognized pathological features of SLE. As a key interferon-stimulated gene, IFI44L was selected as the primary target based on integrated transcriptomic profiles and previous mechanistic evidence, despite several other hub genes exhibiting larger expression fold changes. Correlation analysis demonstrated that elevated IFI44L expression was significantly positively correlated with the proportions of M1 macrophages and activated NK cells, and negatively correlated with naive B cells and neutrophils (all P < 0.001). Dual-cohort ROC analysis confirmed the diagnostic potential of IFI44L, with AUCs of 0.9032 in the training cohort and 0.9550 in the independent validation cohort. Consistent with transcriptomic enrichment results, IFI44L may correlate with type I interferon pathway disturbance and abnormal peripheral immune cell infiltration linked to inflammatory manifestations in SLE. Validated across two independent cross-platform cohorts, IFI44L may serve as a non-invasive diagnostic biomarker for SLE. Its potential as a CAR-T target is merely a theoretical conjecture derived from bioinformatic analysis, which provides preliminary clues for subsequent research on individualized treatment of refractory SLE. Key Points • Cross-platform validation using microarray and RNA-seq datasets verified consistent upregulation of peripheral blood IFI44L in SLE patients. • Elevated IFI44L expression correlates with peripheral blood immune cell infiltration disorders and bioinformatically inferred enrichment of type I interferon associated transcriptional signatures in SLE cohorts. • IFI44L exhibits acceptable diagnostic performance for SLE and may serve as a non-invasive blood-based biomarker for SLE. Its potential as a CAR-T target remains only a bioinformatics-derived hypothesis.

items.title: ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement following surgical aortic valve replacement failure in triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome and systemic lupus erythematosus-associated libman-sacks endocarditis: a case report.
items.abstract: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is a non-infective valvular manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), affecting 15-30% of patients with APS. Characterized by sterile vegetations predisposing to thromboembolism and valvular dysfunction, optimal anticoagulation and intervention strategies remain challenging, particularly with rapid prosthetic failure. A 63-year-old African American man with a 20-year history of SLE and triple-positive APS presented with cardiogenic shock five months after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) for LSE. Echocardiography revealed severe bioprosthetic obstruction (mean gradient 79.6 mmHg, valve area 0.30 cm²). Given prohibitive redo surgical risk (STS-PROM 18.2%), he underwent ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a 26 mm Edwards SAPIEN 3 valve. Left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 25-29% to 55-59% at 4.5 months, sustained at 50-54% at 8-month follow-up. He remained stable on warfarin (INR 2-3), hydroxychloroquine, and rituximab under multidisciplinary care. This case demonstrates diagnostic challenges differentiating LSE from bioprosthetic valve thrombosis (BPVT); a competing diagnosis that could not be excluded without histopathologic confirmation, critical limitations of DOACs in triple-positive APS, and feasibility of ECMO-supported TAVR as an exceptional rescue strategy. Rituximab was administered for refractory APS, though its independent contribution to the favorable outcome cannot be determined. To our knowledge, this is the first reported ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve TAVR following SAVR failure in APS/SLE-associated LSE. It emphasizes multidisciplinary care, warfarin-based anticoagulation, immunosuppression escalation, and long-term surveillance for complex autoimmune valvular disease.

items.title: Golgi-retained TNFR1 variants induce stress-driven inflammation in a subset of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
items.abstract: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) is a complex inflammatory disease characterized by recurrent fevers, arthritis, and systemic hyperinflammation; however, its underlying etiology remains poorly understood. Tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1, TNFRSF1A), the prototypical TNF superfamily receptor, signals through its ligand (tumor necrosis factor, TNF) to activate NF-κB-dependent proinflammatory pathways while also promoting cell death. Through family-based and targeted sequencing, we identified multiple rare TNFRSF1A variants, including a de novo truncating variant in a patient with monophasic sJIA. Integrating single cell RNA-seq with in vitro and ex vivo functional assays, we uncovered a patient-specific, unique monocyte population marked by high inflammatory cytokine production. These cells display impaired endosomal and Golgi trafficking, dysregulated autophagy, and increased markers of cellular stress and immune activation. Confocal microscopy revealed aberrant TNFR1 retention within the Golgi apparatus. These monocytes were refractory to LPS-induced cell death, maintained a M1-like inflammatory phenotype and produced proinflammatory cytokines even at steady state. Despite conferring a loss of function in TNFR1 signaling, these variants paradoxically drive a hyperinflammatory phenotype. We propose that this results from combined effects of reduced TNFR1 signaling and cellular stress induced by retention of the mutant receptor in the Golgi.

items.title: ISarcoPRM-Defined Sarcopenia in Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis: Beyond Disease-Specific Clinical Factors.
items.abstract: To determine the frequency of ISarcoPRM-defined sarcopenia in men with radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA) versus age-matched male controls and to assess associated disease-specific clinical characteristics. In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 108 men with r-axSpA and 108 age-matched male controls were evaluated. ISarcoPRM-defined sarcopenia required reduced handgrip strength, prolonged Chair Stand Test (CST) time, or both, together with a low sonographic thigh adjustment ratio (sTAR). Conditional logistic regression assessed the association with r-axSpA; multivariable logistic regression examined associated factors within r-axSpA. ISarcoPRM-defined sarcopenia was significantly more frequent in men with r-axSpA than in controls (32.4% vs. 7.4%, P <0.001). The adjusted conditional model showed an association between r-axSpA and ISarcoPRM-defined sarcopenia, although imprecisely estimated (adjusted OR 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-108.3; P=0.004). Within the r-axSpA group, older age and higher BMI were independently associated with ISarcoPRM-defined sarcopenia, whereas BASMI-lin and ASAS-HI were not independently associated in the adjusted model. ISarcoPRM-defined sarcopenia was more frequent in men with r-axSpA than in age-matched male controls. Interpretation should consider the cross-sectional design, incomplete characterization of cumulative disease burden, and the potential influence of disease-related lower-extremity limitations and BMI adjustment within the ISarcoPRM algorithm.

items.title: Periodontitis Exacerbates Bone Destruction in Rheumatoid Arthritis Through Porphyromonas gingivalis-Induced Carbamylated Neutrophil Extracellular Traps.
items.abstract: Positive correlations between periodontitis and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) are well-documented, yet the underlying causality and mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to elucidate the causal role of periodontitis in RA progression and to investigate the mechanisms. Here, we identified carbamylated neutrophil extracellular traps (cNETs), a structure closely associated with bone destruction in RA, as a key mediator. Clinically, synovial samples from RA patients with periodontitis exhibited significantly elevated cNET levels compared to those from periodontally healthy RA patients, and cNET abundance positively correlated with higher rheumatoid factor levels, deeper probing depth and greater clinical attachment loss. In a murine model combining periodontitis and RA, periodontitis exacerbated RA severity, accompanied by increased cNETs formation, particularly upon exposure to Porphyromonas gingivalis. Mechanistically, transcriptomic sequencing and functional assays revealed that cNETs promote osteoclastogenesis and aggravate bone erosion in RA by enhancing RANKL secretion via the MAPK pathway. Therapeutically, chemical inhibition of carbamylation markedly reduced ankle joint inflammation and bone destruction, concomitant with decreased cNET levels and MAPK phosphorylation. Together, our findings establish a causal link between periodontitis and RA aggravation, mediated by P. gingivalis-triggered cNETs that fuel osteoclast formation. Targeting cNETs may thus represent a promising therapeutic strategy for RA.

items.title: Significant changes in circulating endocannabinoids correlate with disease severity in rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: To investigate alterations in plasma concentrations of circulating endocannabinoids and endocannabinoid-like molecules in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to assess their associations with the Disease Activity Score 28 with Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (DAS28-ESR). The study was designed as a single-center, cross-sectional investigation. Female patients with RA (n = 43; aged ≥18 years) were recruited at Sheba Medical Center, Israel, and diagnosed according to the 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria. Healthy females (n = 38) served as controls. Plasma levels of 25 endocannabinoids and endocannabinoid-like molecules were quantified using solid-phase extraction followed by electrospray ionization liquid chromatography-high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (ESI-LC-HRMS/MS). Statistical analyses included group comparisons and FDR-corrected linear regression models assessing associations between DAS-28-ESR and metabolite levels, adjusted for age and cannabis use. Several endocannabinoids, including 2-arachidonyl glycerol ether (2-AGE), 2-linoleoyl glycerol (2-LG), 2-oleoyl glycerol (2-OG), 2-palmitoyl glycerol (2-PG), 2-SG, linoleoyl-phenylalanine, linolenic acid (LnA), N-O-leucine, and palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), were significantly elevated in RA patients compared with controls (p = 0.015, p < 0.001, p < 0.001, p < 0.001, p = 0.027, p < 0.001, p = 0.034, p < 0.001, and p = 0.002, respectively). In contrast, anandamide (AEA), N-oleoyl alanine, and O-AEA were significantly reduced (p = 0.012, p < 0.001, and p < 0.001, respectively). Notably, plasma levels of AEA, PEA, and oleoylethanolamide (OEA) correlated significantly with DAS28-ESR scores (p = 0.015, p = 0.008, and p = 0.012, respectively). Specific endocannabinoids and endocannabinoid-like molecules are dysregulated in RA and correlate with disease activity, suggesting potential roles as biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

items.title: [A case of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy complicated with immune thrombocytopenia successfully treated with intravenous immunoglobulin].
items.abstract: A 41-year-old woman diagnosed with polymyositis had been treated with tacrolimus and repeated an intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) over past 14 years, due to worsening symptoms. Preadmission examinations showed thrombocytopenia. We diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) based on positive anti-platelet antibody and increased megakaryocytes on bone marrow examination. Following IVIg, both her muscle weakness and platelet counts normalized. The unique clinical course of this case prompted a reconsideration of her underlying muscular disease. Myopathological reexamination revealed predominantly necrotic and regenerating muscle fibers, and the presence of anti-HMGCR antibodies led to a revised diagnosis of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) with ITP. Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy combined with ITP has been rarely reported. However, there are no prior reports of IMNM complicated with ITP. If thrombocytopenia is documented during the course of treatment in patients with IMNM, the complication of ITP should be taken into account when formulating the treatment strategy.

items.title: Complement inhibition: a therapeutic turning point in the treatment of recurrent myelitis in a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) are autoimmune diseases that have been reported to coexist. We describe the case of a 61-year-old woman with long-standing SLE and Sjögren's disease who developed recurrent longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis associated with concomitant NMOSD. Despite treatment with glucocorticoids, plasma exchange, and rituximab, she experienced multiple neurological relapses, with persistent positivity of anti-aquaporin-4 antibodies and magnetic resonance imaging findings consistent with NMOSD, while SLE remained clinically inactive. Therefore, we initiated treatment with an anti-C5 monoclonal antibody for relapse prevention. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of a patient with coexisting SLE and NMOSD treated with an anti-C5 monoclonal antibody, remaining relapse-free throughout a 22-month follow-up period.

items.title: Salvage Heart Transplantation for Severe Biventricular Failure Associated with Systemic Sclerosis-Rheumatoid Arthritis Overlap Syndrome.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a multisystem autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy and fibrosis, and it often affects the heart, leading to ventricular dysfunction, conduction abnormalities, and arrhythmias. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is also complicated by pericarditis, valvular heart diseases, and diastolic dysfunction. SSc-associated right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a rare but life-threatening condition. Herein, we present a case of SSc/RA overlap syndrome associated with catastrophic biventricular failure mimicking arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy/arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ACM/ARVC), requiring central extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Urgent heart transplantation (HTx) successfully saved the patient's life, and he experienced no rejection, allograft dysfunction, or relapse of SSc/RA post-transplant.

items.title: Metacarpophalangeal Joint Arthroplasty in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Outcomes and Challenges.
items.abstract: Metacarpophalangeal joint (MCP) arthroplasty is a surgical intervention for patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and deformities unresponsive to nonsurgical treatments. This study aims to assess the functional outcomes and complication profile of MCP arthroplasty in patients with SLE. A retrospective study was conducted of patients with SLE who underwent MCP arthroplasty between 2003 and 2019. Clinical data, including demographics, operative indications, complications, and outcomes, were reviewed. Follow-up data were collected through chart reviews and phone interviews. Patient-reported outcome measures, obtained during telephone follow-up, included pain assessed using the visual analog scale, upper-extremity function using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand, and hand appearance satisfaction using the HandQ questionnaire. Thirteen patients with SLE (mean age, 61.92 years) underwent 55 MCP arthroplasties. The main indications for surgery were pain and deformity refractory to nonsurgical treatment. The median follow-up duration was 89.15 months (range, 6.1-259.3 months). After surgery, seven patients had extended follow-up. Complications included eight prosthesis fractures, one infection, and five recurrent deformities. Pain relief was modest (visual analog scale, 2.7/10), functional outcomes were moderate (Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand 47.4), and hand appearance satisfaction was low (HandQ 31/100). MCP arthroplasty in patients with SLE provides moderate, long-term functional improvement and pain relief. However, patient satisfaction with hand appearance remains low. Given the small cohort size and SLE's heterogeneity, further research is needed to optimize long-term outcomes. Therapeutic IV, Retrospective Case Series.

items.title: Acute airway obstruction revealing granulomatosis with polyangiitis: A case report of a rare isolated laryngeal presentation.
items.abstract: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is a rare necrotizing vasculitis predominantly involving the upper respiratory tract, lungs, and kidneys. Isolated laryngeal involvement is rare and may mimic malignancy. We report the case of a 59-year-old man presenting with acute progressive dyspnea and severe airway compromise. Endoscopic examination revealed an infiltrative glotto-subglottic lesion causing marked laryngeal narrowing. Contrast-enhanced cervicothoracic computed tomography demonstrated a heterogeneously enhancing infiltrative soft-tissue mass involving the glotto-subglottic region and anterior commissure without thyroid or cricoid cartilage destruction. Laboratory investigations showed markedly elevated c-ANCA levels. Preservation of the laryngeal cartilaginous framework despite infiltrative soft-tissue thickening may constitute an important radiologic clue favoring GPA. items.title: Microengineering the synovial membrane microenvironment in rheumatoid arthritis research.
items.abstract: It is to synthesize recent advances in microengineered in vitro models of the rheumatoid arthritis synovial microenvironment and evaluate their potential to better recapitulate physiological joint conditions. It discusses current limitations and future directions for improving translational relevance in RA research. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a slow-progressive inflammatory autoimmune disorder characterized by synovial inflammation, hyperplasia, and joint degradation, leading to joint destruction and poor quality of life for patients. Although numerous in vitro models of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have been developed to study disease mechanisms and test therapies, their translational value is limited. Most fail to replicate key features of the in vivo synovial joint, such as its cellular diversity, biomechanical forces, and dynamic cell-matrix interactions. This translational gap underscores the need for advanced 3D microengineered platforms that integrate patient-specific cells, biomechanical elements, and real-time biosensing to bridge in vitro findings to clinical outcomes. Recent progress in microengineering has enabled the development of systems that closely mimic the physiological and pathological conditions of the RA synovial membrane in vitro. This review highlights recent progress in microengineered synovial models and their applications in elucidating RA pathogenesis and seeking therapeutic interventions. We also introduce persisting technical and biological challenges, and emerging trajectories for innovation within this rapidly advancing discipline.

items.title: Association between NT-proBNP levels and future cardiovascular events in systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicenter longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Current strategies for identifying individuals at high risk of cardiovascular events (CVE) in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are lacking. A previous cross-sectional study in SLE showed that NT-proBNP > 133 pg/mL was associated with cardiovascular damage. Our objective was to assess the association between NT-proBNP at a threshold of 133 and incident CVE in SLE. All SLE patients who were included in the randomised controlled trial PLUS between 2007 and 2010 in France were screened. Patients with a history of CVE, an unavailable serum sample at PLUS inclusion, or incomplete follow-up were excluded from the primary analysis. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of CVE during follow-up. A total of 351 patients (out of 573 included in PLUS) were analyzed. Of these patients, 316 (90.0%) were women with a median age of 38 [30-48] years. Among them, 24 (6.8%) patients experienced at least one CVE that occurred a median of 5 [3-7] years after baseline. Five patients had more than one CVE. In the multivariable analysis, age, dyslipidemia and NT-proBNP were significantly associated with the occurrence of CVE. NT-proBNP was >133pg/mL in 22 (6.3%) patients at baseline. The 133 pg/ml threshold was significantly associated with the occurrence of CVE during follow-up (adjusted hazard ratio [CI 95]: 2.94; 95% CI: 1.12-7.71). A NT-proBNP threshold of 133 pg/ml is associated with future CVE in SLE. SLE care guidelines could consider including NT-proBNP measurement in order to better stratify the cardiovascular prevention strategies in this high-risk population.

items.title: Redefining BASDAI cut-offs in axial spondyloarthritis: implications for patients' eligibility for treatment with biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs.
items.abstract: To compare a newly proposed Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) cut-off for high disease activity (BASDAI≥2.5) with the corresponding Axial Spondyloarthritis Disease Activity Score (ASDAS) cut-off (ASDAS≥2.1) as an eligibility criterion for initiating a biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (bDMARD) in routine care patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Real-world patients with axSpA initiating their first bDMARD from 9 European registries were analysed. Patients were categorised into 4 subgroups according to the fulfilment of ASDAS and BASDAI criteria at baseline, and treatment effect was assessed at 6 months using several response and remission outcomes. Adjusted logistic regression analyses were performed to determine whether fulfilling ASDAS and BASDAI criteria was associated with achieving the treatment outcomes. Of 6,329 patients included, 90.9% fulfilled both ASDAS and BASDAI eligibility criteria at baseline, 2.5% and 2.7% fulfilled either ASDAS or BASDAI criterion alone, while 3.8% fulfilled neither. The subgroup fulfilling both criteria demonstrated the highest responses at 6 months, while the highest remission outcomes were observed in the subgroup fulfilling neither criterion. Fulfilling either criterion at baseline was significantly associated with achieving response outcomes at 6 months, whereas a negative association was observed for remission outcomes. In a multinational European cohort, a very large overlap between the BASDAI and the ASDAS eligibility criteria was shown, and the predictive ability of the two criteria to achieve treatment outcomes was comparable. These findings support the use of BASDAI≥2.5 as a criterion for initiating bDMARD therapy in axSpA, particularly when ASDAS is unavailable.

items.title: Pseudoseptic Psoriatic Arthritis With Synovial Leukocytosis > 100,000/μL: A Diagnostic Pitfall Mimicking Iatrogenic Infection.
items.abstract: A 70-year-old woman presented with acute bilateral knee pain and fever following intra-articular injections. Synovial fluid analysis revealed a white blood cell (WBC) count > 100,000/μL, and initial blood cultures grew coagulase-negative staphylococci, suggesting iatrogenic septic arthritis. However, synovial cultures remained negative. Re-evaluation revealed overlooked psoriatic skin lesions and high-titer anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies. The diagnosis was revised to psoriatic arthritis (PsA). This case highlights that PsA can manifest as "pseudoseptic" arthritis with massive synovial leukocytosis. Clinicians should exercise caution in diagnosing septic arthritis based solely on synovial WBC counts, even when the clinical context suggests iatrogenic infection.

items.title: Sex Differences in the Burden of Rheumatoid Arthritis in China, 1990-2021: Trends, Projections to 2050, and Mendelian Randomization of Modifiable Risk Factors.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) disproportionately affects women and imposes a growing burden in an aging China. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2021 (GBD 2021) database, we mapped long-term, sex-stratified trends in RA burden in China vs G20 countries and evaluated genetically supported modifiable risk factors for RA. We analyzed incidence, prevalence, mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and years of life lost (YLLs) for RA, overall and by sex, in China and the G20 from 1990 to 2021. Joinpoint regression and decomposition analysis described historical trends and their drivers. ARIMA models projected burden to 2050 and were cross-validated against Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) projections over the overlapping 2022-2036 horizon. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) examined the causal relationships between six modifiable exposures and RA risk. China's age-standardized prevalence rose from approximately 210 to 245 per 100,000 (AAPC +0.51%), while age-standardized mortality fell (AAPC -0.78%). Female DALYs reached approximately 540,000 person-years in 2021 vs approximately 290,000 in men; age-standardized prevalence in women was roughly 2.2-fold that in men throughout the period. Population aging was the dominant driver of rising absolute burden, accounting for 74.75% of the DALY increment. MR identified elevated body mass index (BMI) and smoking as risk-increasing exposures, and higher physical activity and educational attainment as protective. In European-ancestry sex-stratified analyses, the positive causal effect of BMI appeared stronger in women than in men, though most sex differences did not reach statistical significance; sex-stratified MR estimates for the Chinese Han population were not obtainable. The absolute burden of RA in China is projected to keep rising, driven by population aging, with women carrying the largest share of disability. These findings support sex-informed prevention strategies targeting modifiable exposures such as obesity and smoking, alongside aging-adapted chronic-disease management. Rheumatoid arthritis is a long-term disease in which the immune system attacks the joints, causing pain, stiffness, and lasting damage. It affects women about two to three times more often than men. We wanted to learn how the health burden of this disease in China has changed over three decades, and whether women and men have been affected differently. Using a large international health database, we tracked the disease in China from 1990 to 2021 and compared it with other major economies (the G20). We also used a genetic method to test which lifestyle factors may cause the disease rather than simply being linked to it. The total number of people living with rheumatoid arthritis in China rose sharply. Survival from rheumatoid arthritis improved over time, with fewer deaths recorded across the decades; however, more people were living for extended periods with the disability the disease causes. Women carried a larger and increasingly disabling share of this burden, and population ageing was the main reason the burden grew, especially among older women. Being overweight and smoking raised the risk, while regular physical activity and more education lowered it. These findings suggest that prevention and care should give special attention to women, particularly older women, and should help people manage weight and avoid smoking.

items.title: Clinical Characteristics of Sarcopenia Among SARC-F-Negative Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Sarcopenia is clinically important in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) because chronic inflammation and physical dysfunction may contribute to muscle impairment. Although SARC-F is widely used as a screening tool for sarcopenia, its diagnostic performance in patients with RA remains unclear. This study investigated the agreement between SARC-F and Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 (AWGS2025)-defined sarcopenia and evaluated clinical characteristics of sarcopenia in SARC-F-negative patients with RA. This cross-sectional study included 212 patients with RA enrolled in a prospective cohort. Sarcopenia was diagnosed according to the AWGS2025 criteria. Agreement between SARC-F and AWGS2025-defined sarcopenia was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, overall agreement, and Cohen's kappa coefficient. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed for SARC-F-negative patients. The prevalence of SARC-F positivity was 10.8%, whereas AWGS2025-defined sarcopenia was observed in 25.0% of patients. Overall agreement between SARC-F and AWGS2025-defined sarcopenia was 72.6%, and Cohen's kappa coefficient was 0.10. Among SARC-F-negative patients, 23.3% had sarcopenia. Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that age and Health Assessment Questionnaire-Disability Index (HAQ-DI) were independently associated with sarcopenia. ROC analysis identified an optimal HAQ-DI cutoff value of 0.25. Patients with sarcopenia showed lower walking speed and prolonged Timed Up and Go performance, despite negative SARC-F results. Among SARC-F-negative patients with RA, a substantial proportion met the AWGS2025 diagnostic criteria for sarcopenia and showed impaired physical performance. These findings indicate that a negative SARC-F case-finding result does not necessarily preclude sarcopenia diagnosed according to the AWGS2025 criteria. UMIN Clinical Trials Registry: UMIN000041034.

items.title: Disseminated Cutaneous Tophaceous Gout in a Man With Advanced HIV Disease.
items.abstract: Cutaneous tophi typically develop at periarticular sites in patients with longstanding gout. Widespread dermal deposition of monosodium urate beyond these sites is uncommon and is not recognized as a manifestation of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. We report a 54-year-old man with advanced HIV disease who presented with a ten-year history of progressively enlarging nodules on both lower limbs. HIV had been diagnosed in 2019, and he had been virologically suppressed on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, lamivudine, and dolutegravir since 2020, although his CD4 count remained 34 cells/µL. The lesions were asymptomatic and had not previously been investigated. Examination showed numerous firm, hyperpigmented papules and nodules across both lower limbs together with bilateral olecranon tophi. Serum urate was 0.61 mmol/L, renal function was mildly reduced, and body mass index was 41 kg/m². Punch biopsy demonstrated dermal deposits of amorphous, feathery eosinophilic material bordered by a granulomatous infiltrate, and stains for mycobacteria and fungi were negative. No tissue cultures were obtained; disseminated cutaneous tophaceous gout was diagnosed by clinicopathologic correlation rather than crystal identification. Allopurinol was restarted with dose escalation and colchicine prophylaxis. At six months, the serum urate had fallen to 0.40 mmol/L, within the laboratory reference range but above the target for tophaceous gout, and the tophi had not regressed. This case shows how asymptomatic skin disease can go uninvestigated for years in a patient with a demanding chronic illness. We report the two conditions as coexisting and do not suggest that HIV caused the cutaneous tophi.

items.title: Microscopic Polyangiitis Mimicking Colitis: A Fatal Case of Fulminant Multi-organ Vasculitis.
items.abstract: Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) is a systemic necrotising small vessel vasculitis that predominantly affects the kidneys and lungs. Gastrointestinal (GI) manifestations are less common and may mimic primary enteric disease, delaying recognition of the underlying systemic condition. A 72-year-old woman presented with a one-week history of bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, lower limb oedema, and purpura following recent ibuprofen use. Initial investigations demonstrated severe metabolic acidosis, stage 3 acute kidney injury (AKI), with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 4 mL/min/1.73 m², active urinary sediment, and computed tomography (CT) evidence of extensive colitis with small bowel enteritis. Faecal testing for multiple enteric pathogens, including Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC), and testing for Clostridioides difficile were negative. Strongly positive myeloperoxidase anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (MPO-ANCA; >221.9 IU/mL) supported a diagnosis of ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), while anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibodies were negative. Despite prompt treatment with intravenous (IV) methylprednisolone, cyclophosphamide, therapeutic plasma exchange (PLEX), and intermittent haemodialysis, the patient developed fulminant diffuse alveolar haemorrhage (DAH), refractory hypoxaemia, consumptive coagulopathy, and severe acidaemia. She died on day 8 of admission. Renal biopsy histopathology, reported after death, demonstrated necrotising crescentic pauci-immune glomerulonephritis. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of MPO-ANCA-associated vasculitis presenting with severe gastrointestinal inflammation and bleeding alongside rapidly progressive renal disease. Although the renal findings confirmed ANCA-associated vasculitis, the underlying cause of the gastrointestinal abnormalities remained uncertain, with intestinal vasculitis and ischaemic injury secondary to hypoperfusion among the possible explanations. Recognition of systemic features in patients presenting with gastrointestinal illness and unexplained renal dysfunction is essential to facilitate timely investigation and treatment.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of X-ray- and MRI-based diagnostic pathways in axial spondyloarthritis.
items.abstract: Diagnostic imaging plays a central role in the diagnosis of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Current guidelines recommend a stepwise imaging approach, starting with X-ray and, in negative cases, following with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), are increasingly questioned. The aim of this study is to compare the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of different imaging-based diagnostic strategies for axSpA. A decision-analytic model was developed to evaluate three diagnostic scenarios: (A) initial X-ray screening followed by MRI if negative, (B) a stricter X-ray-based strategy with higher diagnostic thresholds followed by MRI, and (C) direct MRI. A hypothetical cohort of 100000 patients with suspected axSpA and a disease prevalence of 30% was modeled. Different input parameters (prevalence, therapy duration with biologic or targeted disease modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARD) before clinical reassessment, and proportion of patients undergoing therapy escalation with b/tsDMARD) were varied across three scenarios. Cost-effectiveness was expressed as costs per correctly diagnosed axSpA case. Parameter uncertainty was addressed using probabilistic sensitivity analysis with 5000 Monte Carlo simulations and threshold analyses. Unit costs were estimated at 166.91€ for single MRI and 10994.48€ for b/tsDMARD therapy for 11 months. The scenario comparison yielded different break-even values: with MRI costs below 2256€ and b/tsDMARD therapy costs above 682€, scenario C was associated with lower cost. In probabilistic sensitivity analyses, scenario C was economically favorable in 100% of simulations. When varying different input parameters across alternative combinations, these directional trends remained consistent. To support transferability to other health-care systems, we calculated an M R I b / t s D M A R D cost ratio of 0.20 - 0.25. Within and below this range, MRI-based diagnostic pathway is recommended. MRI-based diagnostic pathway represents a clinically and economically balanced alternative to X-ray-based axSpA diagnostics and may be adapted to different healthcare systems. What’s the disease? Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is a chronic inflammatory that mainly affects the spine and joints. It can cause long-term pain and stiffness, and it needs to be caught early so treatment can begin. What’s the problem with current practice? Right now, most guidelines say: start with an X-ray, and only do an MRI if the X-ray looks normal. But X-rays often miss early signs of the disease, meaning some patients go undiagnosed longer than necessary. Researchers are starting to question whether this step-by-step approach is actually the best one. What did we do? We built a mathematical model simulating 100000 imaginary patients suspected of having axSpA, and compared three different approaches: Strategy A: X-ray first → MRI only if X-ray is normal (standard practice) Strategy B: A stricter version of Strategy A, with a higher bar for what counts as a “normal” X-ray → then MRI Strategy C: Skip the X-ray entirely and go straight to MRI What did we find? An MRI scan costs roughly 167€, while the specialist medication used to treat axSpA costs around 11000€ for 11 months. Because missing a diagnosis leads to delayed treatment - and that treatment is very expensive - getting the diagnosis right the first time saves money in the long run. When MRI costs are below ∼2200€ and medication costs are above ∼682€, going straight to MRI is the cheaper overall strategy. In 100% of their simulations, going straight to MRI (Strategy C) came out as the most cost-effective option. We also created a simple ratio (0.20-0.25) to help doctors and health systems in other countries figure out whether this advice applies to them too. What does this mean? In this setting, direct MRI instead of initial X-ray may help avoid missed or delayed diagnoses and may be cost-effective under certain conditions, as a delayed diagnosis can cost more than the MRI itself. However, this depends on the patient group and the local cost setting.

items.title: The paradox of osteoporosis in axial spondyloarthritis: Why antiresorptives may not be enough and anabolic therapy could be prioritized.
items.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) in radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA) exhibits a paradoxical mechanism. Chronic inflammation driven by pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-17A/F, and IL-23) leads simultaneously to accelerated trabecular bone resorption with deterioration of bone microarchitecture and to pathological new bone formation (syndesmophytes, enthesophytes), which locally increases bone mineral density (BMD). As a result, standard dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) significantly underestimates the true fracture risk, which is 2-8 times higher than in the general population. The aim of this narrative review was to discuss the pathomechanisms of OP in r-axSpA, with particular emphasis on the role of key pro-inflammatory cytokines, and to critically evaluate the rationale for using antiresorptive, biological, and anabolic therapies in the context of the specific bone pathology of this disease. The review included original research articles, systematic and narrative reviews, and guidelines published between 2015 and 2025, identified through searches in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus using combinations of keywords related to r-axSpA, osteoporosis, bone microarchitecture (TBS), teriparatide, romosozumab, and inhibitors of TNF-α, IL-17, and JAK. Antiresorptive agents increase BMD but do not interrupt the cytokine-driven catabolic process in trabecular bone, which limits their ability to improve microarchitecture and reduce fracture risk. IL-17A/F inhibitors through effective control of inflammation, exert a beneficial effect on bone metabolism and may slow radiographic progression. Anabolic agents acting primarily via the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, improve not only BMD but, more importantly, bone quality and microarchitecture - making them a potentially more causal treatment option for OP in r-axSpA. Given the dominant role of microarchitectural deterioration, earlier consideration of anabolic agents may be warranted in patients with low trabecular bone score (TBS), abnormal 3D-Shaper results, or low-energy fractures - ideally combined with effective biologic control of inflammation. Prospective clinical trials evaluating this therapeutic strategy are urgently needed.

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy and prognostic value of urinary soluble CD163 in lupus nephritis: a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis : Urinary sCD163 for active lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a major cause of morbidity and progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Current biomarkers, including proteinuria and serological markers, have limited accuracy for detecting active renal inflammation and often fail to reflect intrarenal immune activity. Noninvasive biomarkers are therefore urgently needed. To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and prognostic value of urinary soluble CD163 (uCD163) in patients with LN. We conducted a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis in multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane to evaluate the performance of uCD163 in detecting active LN. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using random-effects models, and overall diagnostic performance was assessed using summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) analysis to obtain a pooled area under the curve (AUC). All statistical analyses were performed using R. We included eight studies with 1,110 participants. uCD163 demonstrated favorable pooled diagnostic performance, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.79-0.94) and specificity of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.81-0.96). The SROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.93. The pooled DOR was 63.37 (95% CI: 14.25-281.75; p < 0.0001). In addition, substantial heterogeneity was observed (I² = 85%), and Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test was borderline at the prespecified threshold (t = -1.95, p = 0.0995), indicating that publication bias or small-study effects cannot be excluded. uCD163 demonstrated favorable diagnostic performance for detecting active lupus nephritis, with high pooled sensitivity and specificity. Despite substantial between-study heterogeneity and the overall low certainty of evidence, these findings suggest that uCD163 may serve as a useful complementary noninvasive biomarker for assessing disease activity.

items.title: Comparative effectiveness and safety of leflunomide versus methotrexate in the treatment of elderly rheumatoid arthritis patients: A retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: The comparative effectiveness and safety of leflunomide and methotrexate in elderly rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients remain understudied despite the growing prevalence of RA in this population. To compare the efficacy, drug survival, and safety of leflunomide and methotrexate in disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARD)-naive RA patients aged ⩾65 years. Retrospective cohort study. Patients aged ⩾65 years with RA who were treated initially with either leflunomide or methotrexate were analyzed. Patients with DMARD-naive RA were selected according to the 2010 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism criteria. Patients received at least 6 months of treatment and were followed up for 24 weeks. Disease activity was assessed using the Disease Activity Score 28 (DAS28)-CRP (remission: DAS28-CRP < 2.6 and low disease activity (LDA): DAS28-CRP 2.6-3.2). Drug survival and adverse events were also recorded. This study included 167 patients (80 on leflunomide and 87 on methotrexate). Methotrexate led to a greater reduction in DAS28-CRP (median reduction 1.9 vs 0.7, p  < 0.001). By contrast, remission (37.9% vs 31.3%, p  = 0.229) and LDA rates (82.8% vs 73.8%, p  = 0.110) were not significantly different. In both groups, swollen joint count was associated with remission ( p  < 0.001). Drug survival rates were comparable in the unadjusted analysis (74.7% vs 66.3%, p  = 0.152). After adjusting for baseline disease activity, methotrexate was associated with a 73% lower hazard of discontinuation (adjusted hazard ratio 0.27, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.13-0.54, p  < 0.001). The adverse event-related discontinuation rate was low and similar between the groups (10% for leflunomide vs 8% for methotrexate, p  = 0.431). Both leflunomide and methotrexate are effective and safe in elderly RA patients. Methotrexate was associated with a greater reduction in disease activity and better adjusted drug survival. However, given the baseline differences in disease activity and the lack of statistically significant differences in remission and low disease activity rates at week 24, methotrexate remains a reasonable first-line option in the absence of contraindications for elderly RA patients. Leflunomide is a viable alternative when methotrexate is not tolerated. Comparing two arthritis medications in older adults: Methotrexate vs. leflunomide This study looked at two common medications (methotrexate and leflunomide) for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in adults aged 65 and older. Commonly, doctors use methotrexate for treating RA initially. This is not always suitable for older patients who have other health problems. We investigated whether leflunomide is a suitable alternative in this age group by comparing the effectiveness and safety of the two drugs over 6 months. We reviewed the medical records of 167 patients aged 65 years with RA who were starting their first-ever RA medication. Eighty patients took leflunomide, and 87 took methotrexate. More patients on methotrexate saw their arthritis activity scores drop significantly. However, by the end of 6 months, there was no difference between patients taking methotrexate and those on leflunomide. The number of patients who reached a state of low disease activity or remission (where symptoms are minimal or gone) was similar in both groups. Additionally, the number of people who stopped their medication was similar for both drugs. However, when researchers accounted for the fact that patients starting methotrexate tended to have more severe arthritis at the beginning, patients were more likely to stay on methotrexate long-term. The results demonstrated that the chance of stopping leflunomide was almost four times higher than stopping methotrexate. Both medications were generally safe. The need to stop either medication due to adverse events was low (10 out of 100 patients on leflunomide and 8 out of 100 patients on methotrexate); some patients on methotrexate experienced nausea, while some patients on leflunomide experienced anemia. For older adults with RA, methotrexate remains the preferred first choice because it powerfully reduces disease activity, and patients are more likely to stay on it. However, leflunomide is a good alternative if methotrexate is not suitable because of other health conditions or side effects.

items.title: Nucleic Acid-Driven Immunopathology in Sjögren's Disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by epithelial dysfunction and pathological lymphocyte homing. Clinically, it manifests with xerostomia, xerophthalmia, and fatigue and may involve systemic features such as arthralgia, cryoglobulinemia, interstitial lung disease, and peripheral neuropathy. Emerging evidence highlights the pivotal role of nucleic acids and their associated receptors in the pathogenesis of SjD. Aberrant nucleic acids can activate type I interferon (IFN-I), the inflammasome, and proinflammatory signaling pathways. This cascade promotes the activation of immune cells and the release of cytokines, thereby exacerbating chronic inflammation. This review article elucidates the mechanisms of nucleic acid-mediated immunopathology in SjD and discusses potential therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Pacific Gout Knowledge in Auckland, New Zealand: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
items.abstract: Objective: Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand experience the highest burden of gout and increased understanding is associated with improved adherence and management. The objective of this study is to assess gout knowledge and identify its associated predictors among Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand. Methods: This cross-sectional study was guided by the Tongan Kakala research framework. Data were collected using a culturally adapted online survey of adults aged 18 years and over living in Auckland, New Zealand. Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analysis were used to show distributions and identify predictors of gout knowledge. Results: A total of 408 Pacific participants were included in this study. Most participants identified as Tongan (43%) or Samoan (36%) and were aged between 18 and 39 years (75.5%). The mean gout knowledge of participants was 4.6 (SD 2.6). Participants demonstrated greater understanding of causes and symptoms of gout, but showed limited knowledge of urate-lowering therapy, target serum urate levels and the life-long treatment of gout. The multivariable linear regression analysis found a significant association between increased gout knowledge and age ( p  < 0.0001), education ( p  < 0.0001), total house-hold income ( p  = 0.03), gout diagnosis ( p  < 0.0001) and obtaining gout information from health professionals ( p  = 0.0003). Conclusion: Our results highlight a significant gap in gout knowledge among Pacific adults in New Zealand, particularly in relation to long-term management. There is a need to develop culturally appropriate and relevant educational approaches co-designed with health professionals, communities and families to improve Pacific peoples' understanding of gout and support adherence and management.

items.title: Synovial and serum S100A4 expression in rheumatoid arthritis is observed across disease stages and synovial pathotypes.
items.abstract: S100A4 promotes proinflammatory and profibrotic pathways. This study aimed to determine if synovial and serum S100A4 protein levels differ between early rheumatoid arthritis (ERA) and established RA (estRA), and among synovial pathotypes. Synovial biopsies from 14 patients with RA were assessed by immunohistochemistry for S100A4 protein expression, along with markers for T cells, T cell subsets, B cells, plasma cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells. Serum concentrations of S100A4 were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Synovial tissue was stratified by pathotype (lympho-myeloid, diffuse myeloid, and pauci-immune). Differences in S100A4 protein expression between groups and correlation with disease activity scores (disease activity score 28-erythrocyte sedimentation rate/C-reactive protein [DAS28-ESR/CRP]) were evaluated. S100A4 was detected in both synovial tissue and serum. Synovial S100A4 staining intensity did not differ between ERA (n = 5) and estRA (n = 9), or across tissue pathotypes. Serum S100A4 levels were also similar between early and established disease. No significant correlations were found between synovial or serum S100A4 levels and DAS28 components (tender/swollen joint counts, ESR, and CRP). In this exploratory study, S100A4 protein expression was consistently detected in RA synovium and serum but did not show clear differences across disease stages or synovial pathotypes, consistent with its proposed proinflammatory and profibrotic roles. These pilot data could support larger-scale study to determine the performance of S100A4 as a biomarker across disease stages and synovial tissue types.

items.title: Fish consumption, omega-3 fatty acids, and risk of developing rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Omega-3 fatty acids, primarily found in fish, have been linked to a reduced risk of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but findings are inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the associations between fish consumption, omega‑3 fatty acids, and RA risk. We searched Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025 for studies examining fish consumption, omega-3 fatty acid intake (dietary or supplemental), or circulating omega-3 levels in relation to RA risk. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% CIs. Evidence certainty was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations framework. The protocol was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251136451). Of 4388 screened records, 13 cohort and 7 case-control studies were eligible for meta-analysis. Fish consumption was associated with a lower risk of RA, with a nonlinear dose-response relationship. Intake of 2 to 3 servings/wk was associated with the lowest risk (RR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.64-0.90 at 2.5 servings/wk), with attenuation at higher intakes (RR 0.97; 95% CI: 0.66-1.43 at 5.5 servings/wk). Similarly, higher dietary omega‑3 intake was associated with lower RA risk (per 1 g/d: RR 0.91; 95% CI: 0.85-0.97). No associations were observed for omega‑3 supplementation (RR 1.09; 95% CI: 0.85-1.40) or circulating omega‑3 levels (RR 0.94; 95% CI: 0.74-1.18); however, these findings were inconsistent and of very low certainty. Evidence suggests that higher fish consumption and intake of dietary omega-3 fatty acids are associated with a lower risk of RA. However, evidence from biomarker studies and supplementation remains limited.

items.title: Impact of infliximab combined with methotrexate on serum inflammatory and immunometabolic biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with metabolic reprogramming of immune cells. Although inflammatory cytokines have been extensively studied, the effects of disease-modifying therapies including methotrexate, infliximab and their combination on serum immunometabolic biomarkers remain incompletely understood. This cross-sectional study included newly diagnosed RA patients, patients receiving MTX monotherapy, patients receiving MTX plus infliximab, and healthy controls. Serum levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-10 (IL-10), lactate, citrate, and succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) activity were measured. Disease activity was evaluated using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints (DAS28). Statistical analyses, hierarchical clustering, correlation and network analyses, principal component analysis (PCA), and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to investigate immunometabolic relationships and treatment-associated changes. Newly diagnosed RA patients showed significantly elevated TNF-α, IL-10, lactate, SDH activity, TNF-α/IL-10 ratio, and DAS28, alongside reduced citrate levels compared with controls and treated patients. Combined MTX and infliximab therapy demonstrated the greatest improvement in inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers and the lowest disease activity. Multivariate analyses identified TNF-α, lactate, and DAS28 as major contributors to disease-associated variation, while citrate displayed an opposing metabolic pattern. Correlation and network analyses identified TNF-α as a central link between inflammation, metabolic remodeling, and disease severity. SEM suggested that treatment-associated reductions in TNF-α were related to decreased glycolytic activity, improved mitochondrial metabolism, and reduced disease activity. RA involves coordinated inflammatory and metabolic dysregulation. Combined MTX and infliximab therapy appears more effective than MTX alone in restoring immunometabolic balance.

items.title: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy complicated by rhabdomyolysis syndrome and central nervous system cytomegalovirus infection: A case report.
items.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) complicated by rhabdomyolysis (RM) syndrome and central nervous system (CNS) infection is extremely rare, difficult to diagnose and associated with a poor prognosis. The present study reports a case of anti-signal recognition particle (anti-SRP) antibody-positive IMNM complicated by RM and CNS cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection to provide a reference for its clinical diagnosis and treatment. The clinical data, laboratory findings, muscle pathology, imaging findings and electromyography results are retrospectively analyzed for a 19-year-old female patient who presented with progressive fatigue and muscle weakness, and the case is discussed in the context of the relevant literature. The patient's serum creatine kinase level peaked at 32,213 U/l, and anti-SRP antibodies were positive. Muscle biopsy revealed myogenic damage with muscle fiber necrosis and C5b-9 deposition. The diagnosis of IMNM was confirmed by muscle biopsy and strongly positive anti-SRP antibodies. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of the cerebrospinal fluid detected CMV with a relative abundance of 100%; however, viral load quantification and read numbers were not available from the assay. Serum CMV-immunoglobulin (Ig)M (213.30 AU/ml; positive) and CMV-IgG (>1,000.00 AU/ml; positive) further supported active CMV infection. The patient's muscle strength progressively improved following combined immunotherapy, antiviral therapy and supportive care. At the 6-month follow-up, upper limb muscle strength had recovered to grade 4+, while lower limb muscle strength had recovered to grade 3. In conclusion, for patients presenting with rapidly progressive muscle weakness and increased muscle enzyme levels, myositis-specific antibodies should be tested for as early as possible. When complicated by a CNS infection, differentiation from Guillain-Barré syndrome is essential. Early comprehensive immunotherapy combined with antiviral therapy may improve the prognosis.

items.title: Comparison of the effectiveness of first- and second-line canakinumab therapy in pediatric colchicine-resistant familial Mediterranean fever: a real-world study.
items.abstract: Comparative data on first-line versus second-line canakinumab following anakinra in pediatric colchicine-resistant familial Mediterranean fever (crFMF) are lacking. We compared effectiveness, flare characteristics, and flare-free survival between treatment sequences. This retrospective single-center cohort study included 89 pediatric patients with crFMF carrying biallelic pathogenic exon 10 Mediterranean Fever gene (MEFV) variants who received canakinumab for at least 6 months, either as first-line therapy ( n  = 48) or following anakinra ( n  = 41). Canakinumab significantly reduced median Pras Disease Severity Score from 8 to 6 and International Severity Scoring System for familial Mediterranean fever from 4 to 1 (both p  < 0.001). Patients receiving first-line canakinumab had fewer attacks during the first 6 months ( p  = 0.014), lower early flare rates (2.1% vs 17.1%; p  = 0.022), and a longer time to first flare (14 vs 10 months; p  = 0.030) than those receiving second-line treatment. Flare-free survival tended to favor first-line treatment (35 vs 19 months; log-rank p  = 0.087), while overall flare rates were similar. Most first flares occurred during dose-interval extension, particularly at 8 weeks. Canakinumab provided effective disease control regardless of treatment sequence. However, patients receiving first-line canakinumab experienced fewer early flares and a longer time to first flare compared with those receiving second-line treatment.

items.title: Use of magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis and monitoring of axial spondyloarthritis in Spain: Perspectives of rheumatologists, radiologists, and patients in a qualitative study.
items.abstract: Axial spondyloarthritis is a chronic inflammatory arthritis that affects the musculoskeletal system. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a technique with both advantages and disadvantages, what leads to inconsistent implementation and use across different healthcare areas. The aim of this study was to assess the current status of the use of spinal and sacroiliac MRI in the diagnosis, management, and follow-up of axial spondyloarthritis by rheumatologists in the Spanish healthcare system. Additionally, the study explored the preferences, opinions and needs METHODS: A qualitative approach was used, consisting of five focus groups with 34 participants and three in-depth individual interviews with a purposive sample that included 24 rheumatologists, six radiologists, and seven patients. Transcripts of the recordings were analysed using a constant comparison method, followed by thematic analysis. Based on the participants' experiences, six thematic areas were identified: (1) diagnosis; (2) management and follow-up; (3) healthcare decisions; (4) variability in prescribing; (5) private healthcare; (6) training and communication needs. In general, there was agreement between the opinions and attitudes expressed by the participating rheumatologists and those of the participating radiologists. The study provides a roadmap of issues to be addressed to improve patient care, primarily: inter-centre differences in access to MRI, difficulties with radiology reports from private practice, and the need for specific training and interdisciplinary communication.

items.title: Early proteinuria reduction as a predictor of long-term renal outcomes in lupus nephritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus associated with substantial risk of end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Early proteinuria reduction has been proposed as a prognostic marker for long-term renal outcomes, yet no quantitative synthesis has pooled the available evidence across independent cohorts. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted of studies reporting proteinuria thresholds at 3, 6, or 12 months as predictors of long-term renal outcomes in biopsy-proven LN. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched. Random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation were used for all pooling. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized using the bivariate Reitsma model and summary receiver operating characteristic analysis. 13 studies (n = 2548) were included. Pooled sensitivity for proteinuria thresholds at 12 months was 0.76 (95% CI 0.67 to 0.83; I 2  = 68.4%) and pooled specificity was 0.83 (95% CI 0.76 to 0.89; I 2  = 0.0%). The 12-month time point demonstrated higher discriminatory performance over 3-month and 6-month assessments. Pooled AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.88) at 12 months, the most precise and most broadly supported estimate across the three time points. For ESRD, the pooled hazard ratio was 3.40 (95% CI 0.98 to 11.80) with substantial heterogeneity (I 2  = 75.5%). Meta-regression was underpowered, and the absence of significant moderators should not be read as evidence that the covariates tested do not modify effect. These findings provide a quantitative foundation for the 12-month treat-to-target milestone in current guidelines, and they identify 12-month proteinuria as a candidate surrogate endpoint that now warrants formal trial-level evaluation. They do not establish it as a validated surrogate, and it should not be used as one until that evaluation has been carried out.

items.title: Machine Learning-Driven ZnO NRs@Ag SERS Platform for Rheumatoid Arthritis Liquid Biopsy in a Multicenter-Recruited Cohort.
items.abstract: The analytical chemistry diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) faces challenges such as the time lag of conventional serological assays and matrix masking in complex biofluid analysis. This study proposes a label-free liquid biopsy framework integrating band-regulated surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing with machine learning algorithms. Experimental characterizations (XPS and TRPL) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the ZnO NRs@Ag heterojunction drives efficient spatial separation of charge carriers via stepped band alignment. This achieves a deep synergy between electromagnetic (EM) and chemical enhancements (CM), significantly improving the signal selectivity of metabolites against high-abundance backgrounds. Meanwhile, the substrate exhibits good batch-to-batch structural reproducibility and environmental storage stability. Based on this sensing platform, a patient-level internal validation was conducted on a multicenter-recruited serum cohort. By averaging replicate spectra to prevent data leakage, the model classification was strictly performed on 74 independent patient-level input features (comprising 66 RA cases and 8 healthy controls). Under a leave-one-patient-out cross-validation architecture coupled with dynamic in-fold oversampling, the linear classification model (PLS-DA) achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.9337. Furthermore, utilizing the SHAP method, the model identified putative spectral features that influenced the classification decision, providing a reference for exploring related pathological metabolic changes. This study elucidates the synergistic enhancement mechanism of the heterojunction at the electronic state level and verifies the preliminary diagnostic potential of the platform in decoding high-dimensional metabolic profiles, offering a methodological foundation for applying SERS technology to autoimmune disease screening.

items.title: Real-world avacopan use in ANCA-associated vasculitis: glucocorticoid exposure and healthcare resource utilization from US claims data.
items.abstract: Avacopan is an adjunctive therapy for severe active granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis. We evaluated treatment patterns, glucocorticoid exposure and healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) among adults initiating avacopan, including a sub-cohort aged 65+. This retrospective claims analysis utilized Medicare Fee-for-Service and MORE2 Registry® databases. Adults initiating avacopan with 12 months of continuous enrolment before and after index (first claim) were included. Among patients persistent (no ≥ 90-day gap) on avacopan, changes in prednisone-equivalent daily dose (PEDD) and HCRU were evaluated over 12 months in the primary cohort and a 65+ sub-cohort. Of 167 patients (median age 55 years), 53 (31.7%) were age ≥ 65 years. Among patients persistent on avacopan (n = 94), mean PEDD decreased from 12.6 mg/day during the 90 days pre-index to 5.1 mg/day at 12 months post-index in the primary cohort (n = 94), and from 15.1 to 6.9 mg/day in the 65+ sub-cohort (n = 25). In the primary cohort, the proportion of patients with emergency department visits decreased from 62.8% to 39.4%, and inpatient admissions from 55.3% to 21.3%. These reductions were also observed in the 65+ sub-cohort, where both emergency department visits and inpatient admissions declined from 60.0% and 68.0%, respectively, at baseline to below reporting thresholds at follow-up. In this real-world analysis, avacopan use was associated with reduced glucocorticoid exposure and lower HCRU over 12 months among patients who remained on treatment. These trends were also observed in patients aged 65+. Longer-term comparator studies are needed.

items.title: Comparative risk of serious psychiatric events with belimumab versus oral immunosuppressant use in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare the risk of serious psychiatric outcomes among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus initiating belimumab versus oral immunosuppressants.MethodsWe emulated a target trial using observational data from TriNetX electronic health records database to compare the risks of serious psychiatric events among patients with non-renal SLE initiating belimumab or an oral immunosuppressant (azathioprine, methotrexate, or mycophenolate). Propensity score overlap weighting was used to emulate randomization. The main outcomes were hospitalization for depression and suicide attempt or self-harm. In a per-protocol analysis, we used inverse probability of treatment weighting to adjust for adherence to assigned treatment. A secondary analysis assessed new-onset depression.ResultsWe compared 2434 and 5644 initiators of belimumab and azathioprine, 2163 and 7224 initiators of belimumab and methotrexate, and 2431 and 6350 initiators of belimumab and mycophenolate, respectively. After weighting, baseline covariates were balanced across groups; 95% of patients were female and mean age was 44 years. Belimumab was not associated with an increased risk of hospitalization for depression compared with azathioprine, methotrexate, or mycophenolate. Suicide attempt or self-harm were rare. There was no difference in the risk of new-onset depression among patients without prior mood disorder.ConclusionAmong patients with non-renal SLE, belimumab was not associated with increased risk of serious psychiatric events compared with commonly used oral immunosuppressants, supporting its safety in clinical practice.

items.title: Clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of rheumatoid arthritis-associated lymphoproliferative disorders in the era of biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: a multicenter retrospective study.
items.abstract: This multicenter retrospective study evaluated the clinicopathological features, prognostic factors, and evolution of rheumatoid arthritis-associated lymphoproliferative disorders (RA-LPD) treatment in the biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (b/tsDMARD) era. We analyzed 217 patients diagnosed at eight Japanese institutions. Spontaneous regression was observed in 30.4% of patients with RA-LPD. Extranodal involvement was significantly more common in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)-type, whereas Epstein-Barr virus positivity was higher in classical Hodgkin lymphoma (CHL)-type. DLBCL-type demonstrated superior progression-free survival (PFS) compared to CHL-type, while overall survival (OS) was comparable. Histological subtype was the sole independent predictor of PFS. Multivariate analysis identified low hemoglobin levels, elevated lactate dehydrogenase levels, and poor performance status as independent adverse prognostic factors for OS. Post-LPD diagnosis, methotrexate was discontinued in most patients, followed by an increased use of b/tsDMARDs. Transitioning to b/tsDMARDs represents a feasible strategy to balance RA control and oncological safety.

items.title: Small Cell Lung Cancer Developing After Regression of Clinically Suspected Methotrexate-Associated Lymphoproliferative Disorder: A Diagnostic Pitfall in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Methotrexate-associated lymphoproliferative disorder (MTX-LPD) is a complication of methotrexate therapy in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Distinguishing suspected MTX-LPD from a new malignancy can be challenging when thoracic lesions appear after regression of earlier lesions. In a 69-year-old man with RA, MTX-LPD was clinically suspected but not histopathologically confirmed during methotrexate therapy. Multiple pulmonary nodules, bilateral adrenal masses and an anterior chest wall lesion regressed after methotrexate withdrawal and corticosteroid therapy. Prednisolone was increased to prevent worsening of RA after methotrexate withdrawal. Approximately 15 months later, he presented with dyspnoea and chest computed tomography revealed multiple right pleural nodules, pleural thickening and pleural effusion. The pleural lesions differed in distribution from the initial abnormalities. Pleural fluid cytology suggested small cell carcinoma and computed tomography-guided biopsy established a diagnosis of small cell lung cancer. Chemotherapy with carboplatin and etoposide resulted in tumour regression and reduced pleural effusion. This case emphasizes that regression following methotrexate withdrawal does not establish MTX-LPD and that new or atypical thoracic lesions warrant renewed diagnostic assessment and tissue confirmation.
